verdict.rationale: CoreWeave documents several of its own ways to get data out: AI Object Storage offers S3-compatible access and lets you download objects from the Cloud Console, usage can be exported through the FOCUS API (Public Preview), and clusters are standard Kubernetes reachable with kubeconfig/kubectl. However, there is no documented account-wide export, offboarding path, or data-portability guarantee, so 'all of my data' and 'leave' are only implied. missing for 10: a documented full-account data export or offboarding/migration process, egress terms for leaving, a GA (not preview) usage export, and independent or hands-on corroboration of migrating off.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: Store training data, checkpoints, and model weights with efficient S3-compatible access directly to your GPU compute resources.
You can now browse, upload, download, and manage objects in CoreWeave AI Object Storage buckets directly from the CoreWeave Cloud Console
You can also export usage programmatically with the FOCUS API (Public Preview)
CoreWeave Kubernetes Service (CKS) offers a managed Kubernetes service that lets you run clusters on bare metal servers in CoreWeave Cloud.
Create and download a kubeconfig for a specific cluster, so you can interact with the cluster using commands like kubectl.
